test_title: SSC CPO Tier-II Previous Year Paper (Held On: 8th November 2021)
subject: general
question:
**Select the most appropriate direct form of the given sentence.**

A worker told his companion that he was totally exhausted and couldn’t walk anymore.

options.text: A worker said to his companion, “He was totally exhausted and couldn’t walk anymore.”
A worker said to his companion, “I am totally exhausted and cannot walk anymore.”
A worker said to his companion, “He is totally exhausted and couldn’t walk anymore.”
A worker said to his companion, “I was totally exhausted and couldn’t walk anymore.”

solution:
The correct answer is- 'A worker said to his companion, “I am totally exhausted and cannot walk anymore.”'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To change the sentence to a direct speech we need to follow the following steps:

 
 
• In the reporting speech, replace the verb '*told*' with '*said to/says*'.
 
• We know that when the reporting speech is in the *past indefinite *change it to *present indefinite.*
 
• The *model verb *'**could**' will change to **can.**
 
• The conjunction '*that*' should be replaced by an inverted comma, enclosing the reported speech.
 
• The pronoun *she* will change to *I*. 
 
 
 
• Thus according to the given steps, *option 2 *is the correct answer.

And the correct sentence is: *A worker said to his companion, “I am totally exhausted and cannot walk anymore.”*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** ​

 
• Here are some rules that should be followed while converting an indirect speech to direct speech:

 
 
• Use the reporting verb such as (*say, said to*) in its correct tense.
 
• Put a comma before the statement and the first letter of the statement should be in capital letter.
 
• Insert *question marks*, *quotation marks*, *exclamation marks *and *full stop*, based on the mood of the sentence.
 
• Remove the conjunctions like (*that, to, if *or *whether*) wherever necessary.
 
• Where the reporting verb is in the past tense in indirect, change it to present tense in the direct speech.
 
• Change the past perfect tense either into present perfect tense or past indefinite tense, as necessary.
